questions.title: Section B, Question 1

prompt.en:
The input to the following program segment will be 99 distinct integers between 1 and 100 (inclusive).

Complete function f() so that it returns the integer between 1 and 100 (inclusive) that does not appear in the input.

Assume that a is an array of 100 integers and k is an integer between 0 and 100 inclusive.

Complete the procedure swap so that it swaps the values of a[x] and a[y]. You must NOT make use of the procedures f or g.

Assume that a is an array of 100 integers and k is an integer between 0 and 100 inclusive.

Complete the procedure f so that it reverses the first k elements in the array a.

Assume that a is an array of 100 integers and k is an integer between 0 and 100 inclusive.

Complete the procedure g so that it reverses the last k elements in the array a. You may make use of the procedures swap and f.

Consider a rectangular grid, where the cell labeled with S is the starting-point, cell labeled with T is the target-point, and cells labeled with C are the checkpoints. We call a path an interesting path if and only if it is a path that walk from the starting-point to the target-point by repeatedly walking to either the cell below or on the right, and passing through EXACTLY ONE checkpoint.

Now consider the 5 × 5 grid below: (cell A1 labeled as S and cell E5 labeled as T)

On the answer sheet, label exactly TWO cells as checkpoints (C) so that the number of distinct interesting paths is EXACTLY 2.

figure.alt: The printed 5 by 5 grid, columns A to E and rows 1 to 5, with S at A1 and T at E5.

prompt.en: Consider a string that consists of 100 lowercase letters. You may remove an arbitrary number of characters in the string without changing the order of the remaining characters. In the worst case, at least how many characters should you remove so that the remaining string is a palindrome? (Hint: Palindromes are strings that read the same forward or reversed. For example, “ABBA” is a palindrome while “ABCD” isn’t.)
Complete the function f(x) so that the function g(ch) can convert lowercase letters to uppercase and vice versa. For example, g('A') should return a and g('q') should return Q.

questions.title: Section B, Question 6

prompt.en:
Complete the function find_sum() so that it returns the sum of all positive numbers in num[0..99]. You may assume that the values stored in num[0..99] are integers between -100 and 100 inclusive.

Special rule: Your answers are NOT allowed to include any of the following characters: <, > and =.

targets.helperSource: int abs(int x) { return x < 0 ? -x : x; }

prompt.en:
It is guaranteed that n is an integer between 1 and 100 inclusive.

Complete the function is_prime(n), so that is_prime(n) returns 1 if n is a prime, and 0 otherwise.

It is guaranteed that n is an integer between 1 and 100 inclusive.

Complete the function prime_count(n), so that prime_count(n) returns the number of primes between 1 and n (inclusive).

prompt.en: The input to the following program is 100 integers between 0 and 10000 inclusive. The program tries to output the number of distinct integers in the input. However, the program contains an error that can be fixed by changing exactly one line. Find the line and correct it.
